title: Seven adoption benefit files lacked a documented supervisor review

beats.text: Every two years, California required a fresh look at an adoption assistance benefit.
San Francisco also required a supervisor to check the caseworker’s reassessment.

visual.kicker: When an adoption benefit needs review

beats.text: Auditors selected 60 participants from a population of 1,087.

visual.kicker: Seven files lacked proof of supervisor review

beats.text: Seven files lacked evidence of the supervisor’s review.
The agency described difficulty accessing paper files during the pandemic.

visual.kicker: Seven files lacked proof of supervisor review

beats.text: The auditors checked whether eligibility had actually ended.
None of the seven cases met an event that ended eligibility.
The audit identified no questioned costs.
The FY2024 report marked the correction implemented.

visual.kicker: The next report documented the correction

beats.text: The agency trained staff and converted its files to digital format.

visual.kicker: The next report documented the correction

beats.text: Supervisors could use monthly reports to track the renewals.
A later check could show whether reviewers kept documenting those decisions.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
